title: Plenty of dumplings, an untouched mouth
odia:
ଛ’ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳ ଗଇଁଠା
ପାଟି ହୋଇ ନାହିଁ ଅଇଁଠା।
literal_meaning: Dumplings from six ada measures of rice; the mouth has not even been soiled by eating.
meaning_odia: ଛଅ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳର ଗଇଁଠା, ଅଥଚ ପାଟି ଅଇଁଠା ହୋଇନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏହି ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ରହିଛି। ଅଡା ଏକ ଶସ୍ୟମାପ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏତେ ଖାଦ୍ୟକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ କିଛି ଖାଇବାରେ ଗଣନା ନକରିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗକୁ କଥାଟି ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିପାରେ। କିଏ କେତେ ଖାଇଲା, ପାଠ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କହୁନାହିଁ।
explanation: A measured quantity of rice dumplings stands beside a mouth said to be untouched by eating. One editorial reading hears a teasing refusal to count plenty as even a taste. The verse leaves the eating itself unstated, so the contrast can be appreciated without inventing a meal or judging anyone’s actual hunger.
usage_example: Original imagined example for this reading: Someone receives a substantial share of something and dismisses it as practically nothing. A listener recalls the dumplings that supposedly have not even touched the mouth.
cultural_context: ଗଇଁଠା and ଅଇଁଠା rhyme, connecting the food with the mouth’s claimed condition. The measure in the first line gives weight to what the second line appears to dismiss.

witnesses.locator: Page19, couplet beginning ଛ’ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳ ଗଇଁଠା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; wording and two-line layout retained. ଅଡା rendered as ada grain measure without conversion. First line has no explicit eating verb; expanded interpretation is editorial.

graphic.alt: A woman raises a palm beside a plate of rice dumplings while another diner looks on.
graphic.caption: An imagined exchange puts abundant dumplings beside a dismissive response.

odia_summary: ଅନେକ ଗଇଁଠା ସହ ପାଟି ଅଇଁଠା ନହେବାର ଅସଙ୍ଗତି।
english_summary: A substantial quantity is set against a supposedly untouched mouth.
